deep.reconstruction: This page has no text. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 file on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites' (pseudoline arrangements in the real projective plane), and it holds three sketches. (1) Top left, in ink: an arrangement of five straight lines in 'star' position, with a pencil line nearly duplicating one of them. It looks like a test configuration of five lines in general position, close to the pentagram arrangement, in which each line meets the other four once. (2) Top centre: a disk/ellipse model. The boundary carries marked points, and two heavy points sit at top and bottom. In the disk model of RP^2 boundary points are identified antipodally, so the two heavy points probably represent a single point. A fan of pseudolines runs through that point, which is in effect a pencil, or 'parallel class', of pseudolines through a point at infinity. Other pseudolines cross the fan, their crossings are marked as vertices of a near-grid, and some cells along the boundary are hatched (perhaps triangular or unbounded cells). This is the familiar picture of an arrangement swept by, or extended by, a pencil, closely related to wiring diagrams and allowable sequences. (3) Bottom, mostly faint pencil: a large network of pseudolines carrying arrows, which suggests orientations of the lines or a sweep/flow direction. In the lower part one dashed pseudoline passes through several marked points, each a crossing of two or more other lines. The largest point has a curved arrow beside it and hatched wedges next to it. The likely reading is a multiple (non-simple) intersection point being studied by turning one line about it: a local perturbation that resolves the multiple point into simple crossings, or a triangle flip (Ringel-type mutation) that moves a line across a vertex. Overall the page is exploratory drawing on combinatorial pseudoline geometry: pencils of pseudolines, multiple points on a line, and local moves. Nothing on the page states or proves a result.

ideas.what: Disk model of the projective plane with a pencil of pseudolines through one (antipodally doubled) boundary point, crossed by other pseudolines

ideas.modern_name: Perturbation of non-simple arrangements; triangle flips / mutations

deep.surprise_reason: These are exploratory drawings of standard pseudoline configurations (pencils, multiple points, local moves) and contain no stated result. They document Grothendieck's hands-on engagement with the subject but add nothing new beyond Ringel, Grünbaum and Goodman–Pollack.
transcription_corrections: The isolated mark '"' near the top centre is a small pair of strokes beside a faint pencil arrow (possibly 'll'), not a quotation.
The bottom drawing contains many faint pencil arrows along the pseudolines and hatched wedges at the large marked point and in boundary cells of the disk; these are worth noting in the description.
